_meta.classical_seed_check: all 8 classical anchors identified by tableau content-hash; each appears exactly once, at cycle_id 0 / seed 0
_meta.schema: top-level key per finding; each finding has 'verdict' (honest one-liner), 'numbers' (scalar facts), 'series' (chart-ready arrays; non-empty or {'absent': reason})

efficiency.verdict: Yes. At the shared 65,536-cycle budget under floor-rounded Q15, 16 of 16 archive cells holding a discovered method beat every classical anchor of equal or lower per-step cost on held-out error; the best discovered method (order 2, 3 stages, 22 cycles/step) reaches held-out error 0.0286 against 0.0844 for the best classical anchor (midpoint), a 3.0x reduction. The remaining classical cells are euler (sole order-1 entry) and rk38, which no discovered 4-stage order-4 method displaced in its own cell.

numbers.note_on_comparison: Every heldout_error is evaluated at the same total budget of 65536 cycles, so cheaper methods take more steps; 'cycles' is the per-step coefficient-arithmetic cost at n_states=1 under m0plus_fast. The cheapest anchor with the lowest error is midpoint (11 cycles), which is cheaper than every discovered elite, so beating all cheaper-or-equal anchors here equals beating every anchor outright.
caveats: Cell elites are selected by held-out error among 45k+ unique candidates, so the champion values carry selection (winner's curse) bias; the CMA-ES search itself optimizes only the search-set error.

Tier labels are mechanical insertion-time comparisons against the then-incumbent, not a validation grade of the final elite: the best cell's elite cleared neither tier above its own, and both of those start from a lower search error than the incumbent's. The vocabulary now writes that case no_improvement and an empty cell no_incumbent; records written before the split, this one included, still carry the merged word 'unreplicated'.
rc_thermal saturates near 0.156 for every classical method (see rc_thermal_collapse), so classical held-out RMS values are floored near 0.078; discovered winners break that floor.

series.chart_hint: log-log scatter, x=cycles, y=heldout_error, color by kind, label classical points by name

floor_bias_flip.verdict: Floor rounding reorders the field at the 65,536-cycle budget. On the three search problems euler's RMS error is 0.0129 under floor against 0.0590 for rk4 (4.6x worse), while under round-to-nearest rk4 has the lower error (0.0289 against 0.0469): euler moves from rank 3 to rank 1 and rk4 from rank 2 to rank 4 of 4. Over all 7 problems rk38 stays first in both modes, but the floor-mode spread between methods collapses.

numbers.dahlquist_note: Under floor, euler/heun2/rk38 hit dahlquist error 4.539993e-05, which equals exp(-10), the full reference value: the Q15 state decays to exactly 0 and the true answer is below one LSB, so floor's downward bias lands on the right answer. Under round-to-nearest the state stalls in a dead zone above zero (errors 0.033 to 0.092, up to 2032x worse).
numbers.mechanism: Each Q15 multiply floors, injecting a -0.5 LSB expected bias per product. rk4 spends more multiplies per unit of simulated time and takes larger steps at equal budget, so its order advantage is spent absorbing bias; cheap low-order methods take more, smaller steps and win on problems whose solutions decay.

series.chart_hint: paired bars or slope chart per problem, log y; a second slope chart for aggregate ranks (search_rms)

crossover.verdict: On damped_osc, rk4's Q15 error decouples from its float truncation error at h = 0.15625 (float error keeps falling as h^4; Q15 error rises from 1.13e-03 to 2.58e-02 as h shrinks to 0.0097656); heun2 decouples later, at h = 0.039062. The stored falsification verdict is 'mixed': coefficient arithmetic is 50-56% of per-step cycles on m0plus_fast (above the 0.30 proceed threshold) but 14.8% for heun2 on m0plus_slow (below the 0.15 kill threshold). At the equal 65,536-cycle budget under floor, rk4 wins 0 of 7 problems outright (under round-to-nearest: 1 of 7, with rk38 taking 5).

rk4_wins_at_budget.note: computed from floor_round.json over the four methods it covers (euler, heun2, rk4, rk38) at budget 65536, m0plus_fast

series.chart_hint: log-log lines, x=h, y=error; per method one solid (q15_error) and one dashed (float_error) line; null q15 values are overflow (error was infinite)

rc_thermal_collapse.verdict: All 8 classical methods land within 1.6% of one another on rc_thermal under floor (errors 0.1558 to 0.1582) because every one of them drives the Q15 state into a dead zone 4 to 18 LSBs from the origin while the true solution still has norm 0.1592: the reported error is essentially the reference itself, a quantization floor, not a method property. Under round-to-nearest the same methods separate (rk38 reaches 0.0511), and the best discovered method reaches 0.0205 while still using floor.

numbers.mechanism: rc_thermal decays toward equilibrium and its derivative is stored scaled by 1/8 (DERIV_SCALE), so late in the run the quantized derivative terms are a few LSBs; floor rounding turns them into extra decay, and every classical method's state collapses to near zero instead of tracking the slow mode. Error metric is ||y - ref(4)||/peak, so everyone reports about ||ref(4)|| = 0.159 minus a small residual.

series.chart_hint: grouped bars per method: floor_error vs round_error, with a horizontal line at reference_norm

phase0_exhaustive.verdict: Closed result: the phase-0 space (2-stage, a21 on the dyadic lattice s<=6, |a21|<=2: 256 candidates, 16 with exactly representable b) was enumerated in full and all 16 members are in the archive. Nothing in it improves on a21 = -1/8, b = (5/1, -4/1) at 15 cycles/step with held-out error 0.0613, a near-tie with a21 = -1/4 (0.0614); within the same family midpoint ranks 7 and heun2 ranks 12 of 16. The optimum also has a lower held-out error than all 8 classical anchors (best: midpoint, 0.0844) at the equal budget.

rank_stability.note: Each variant re-ranks every member over the three problems it keeps. The full-set column reproduces the published ranking.

numbers.closure_note: Phase 0 is exhaustive by construction (events.jsonl records 'enumeration complete'), so this optimum is over the whole space, not a sample: no 2-stage tableau in the lattice does better at this budget under these semantics.

series.chart_hint: dot plot: x=a21 (categorical, ordered by value), y=heldout_error, highlight optimum, midpoint, heun2

search_progress.verdict: The archive's best held-out error has stepped down 5 times in 3,931 cycles, at 0, 1, 4, 6, 33. The step at cycle 0 is a seeded classical method, so the search itself has lowered the number 4 times, most recently at cycle 33, 3,897 cycles ago. The run's saturation check still reads CONTINUE. The saturation check reads the accepted-record events rather than this number. It asks whether any cell has taken a new elite, improved the one it held, or accepted a record at the heldout_verified tier inside its window, and it can only return SATURATING once the falsification run has been published. CONTINUE therefore means the grid is still moving somewhere, not that the best held-out error has moved.

numbers.note_on_counting: A step is a cycle whose best held-out error is lower than every earlier cycle's. Counting steps over the raw record order instead counts the order the cycle-0 seeds were written and reports eight.
numbers.note_on_saturation: The saturation check reads the accepted-record events rather than this number. It asks whether any cell has taken a new elite, improved the one it held, or accepted a record at the heldout_verified tier inside its window, and it can only return SATURATING once the falsification run has been published. CONTINUE therefore means the grid is still moving somewhere, not that the best held-out error has moved.

series.chart_hint: step plot, x=cycle_id, y=heldout_error, log y

side_tracks.verdict: 103 off-archive points measured across 10 jobs on 2 tracks, each stating its own arithmetic. All are outside the scored path and none carries Q15 quantization, so none is comparable with an archive error. 40 of them were measured again after the executor changed.

adaptive.controller_gains.arithmetic: float64 only; no Q15 effects are included
adaptive.controller_gains.closes: EPOCH2-DESIGN section 4: the dyadic PI gains rest on one measurement, and the classical alpha for a 3(2) pair is 1/3 rather than 1/4
adaptive.controller_gains.schema: one entry per reference problem at a fixed tolerance, under the given PI controller gains; the epoch-2 question is which dyadic gains to freeze into the Q15 controller table

adaptive.pair_census.arithmetic: exact over Fractions; no float and no Q15 arithmetic is involved
adaptive.pair_census.closes: EPOCH2-DESIGN section 2: the search-space note assumes a dyadic A admits both an order-p b and an order-(p-1) b_hat with a free parameter left, and that has not been counted
adaptive.pair_census.schema: counts over every strictly lower-triangular dyadic A at this stage count and lattice size: how many admit an order-3 weight vector, how many admit an order-2 vector with a free column left (so that the embedded estimate is not forced to zero), how many are FSAL, and how many have an exactly representable order-2 vector. A space larger than the cap is reported rather than walked.

adaptive.q15_estimate_floor.arithmetic: Q15 fixed point throughout, on the pinned primitives in rk_harness.fixedpoint, with floor multiply; the reference float mode used to reproduce the frozen curve is float64
adaptive.q15_estimate_floor.closes: EPOCH2-DESIGN section 3: the roughly 2 LSB floor-bias figure for the Q15 error estimate is an estimate, and section 5 needs the scored tolerance ladder to sit above whatever that floor turns out to be
adaptive.q15_estimate_floor.schema: one document per (validation problem, scale factor): the exact error weights and their fixed-point representation, a tolerance ladder in LSB of the scaled state run under both controller tables, the measured floor statistics of the estimate, the Q31 time register terms, and the ARMv6-M reference sequence priced under all three cost models

adaptive.suite_sweep.arithmetic: float64 only; no Q15 effects are included
adaptive.suite_sweep.closes: EPOCH2-DESIGN section 5: the scored tolerance ladder is unchosen, and the published curve covers 3 of the 8 validation problems
adaptive.suite_sweep.schema: one entry per tolerance: status, and when the run finished, the accepted/rejected step counts, the exact function-evaluation count (FSAL reuse included) and the final error under the T8 metric

sdirk.gamma_a21_scan.arithmetic: tableau and stability algebra exact over Fractions; the measured order is float64
sdirk.gamma_a21_scan.closes: EPOCH3-DESIGN: the L-stability window in J4 is 17 candidates wide and nothing pins that width, and the second free parameter of the 2-stage SDIRK is never varied
sdirk.gamma_a21_scan.schema: one row per kept gamma at this denominator exponent: the exact stability data, which belongs to gamma alone, and the a21 from the second axis with the smallest order-3 residual, with its b, the exactness and CSD weight of that b, stiff accuracy and the measured order on dahlquist

sdirk.gamma_dyadic_scan.arithmetic: tableau and stability algebra exact over Fractions; the measured order is float64
sdirk.gamma_dyadic_scan.closes: EPOCH3-DESIGN: L-stability is to be checked numerically for the snapped gamma, and the NOT_L_STABLE threshold is a placeholder
sdirk.gamma_dyadic_scan.schema: one row per dyadic gamma near 1 - sqrt(2)/2 at this denominator exponent: the exactly solved order-2 tableau, its L-stability margin |R(inf)|, whether it is A-stable, and its measured order on dahlquist

sdirk.jacobian_cost.arithmetic: float64 only; no Q15 effects are included
sdirk.jacobian_cost.closes: EPOCH3-DESIGN: the optional analytic Jacobian field is unpriced because every side-track SDIRK number is costed with the finite difference
sdirk.jacobian_cost.schema: the analytic Jacobian and the one-sided finite difference, sampled as whole matrices at two fixed states, then the same fixed-step SDIRK2 run with each of them at three step counts, plus the per-step cycle estimate under both

sdirk.newton_iters.arithmetic: float64 only; no Q15 effects are included
sdirk.newton_iters.closes: EPOCH3-DESIGN: three Newton iterations is the prototype's setting, not a ruling
sdirk.newton_iters.schema: measured order on dahlquist plus stiff-suite error and per-step cycle estimate at a fixed modified-Newton iteration count

sdirk.stiff_suite.arithmetic: float64 only; no Q15 effects are included
sdirk.stiff_suite.closes: EPOCH3-DESIGN: the stiff case rests on rc_thermal and a synthetic two-rate system, while the suite now has three purpose-built stiff problems
sdirk.stiff_suite.schema: step count vs error for the explicit anchors and SDIRK2 on one stiff member of the T8 validation suite; a diverged entry is a result, not a gap

sdirk.stiff_suite_budget.arithmetic: float64 only; no Q15 effects are included
sdirk.stiff_suite_budget.closes: EPOCH3-DESIGN: the stiff ladder in J3 stops at 256 steps while the harness scores at a matched cycle budget, where the cheap explicit methods take thousands of steps
sdirk.stiff_suite_budget.schema: per method, the step count that BUDGET_CYCLES buys on this problem, the error there, and a ladder of a quarter, a half, one, two and four times that count with the analytic cycles each rung would cost; a diverged rung is a result, not a gap

series.chart_hint: table per job; there is no shared axis across jobs
